method: Assembled on 2026-11-11 by one assembling agent that ran the research passes one after another, each pass enumerating its own publishers in announcement-date order inside the window and taking events in that order. No pass consulted asktherecruiter.com, this repository, the tracker database or its source registry. Discovery was public web search and the publishers' own listing pages and sitemaps, read only where the site's robots.txt allows an automated reader (sites that refuse one, including some national dailies and the main US startup wires, were not used). Every row cites the original publisher: the company's own release, an exchange or company announcement, or a named outlet's own article. Every source page was fetched and the company, date, place and amount were read on the page before the row was written, and every URL was fetched again mechanically before sealing (all answered HTTP 200). Nothing was added, edited or removed after matching began, because matching has not begun. Passes were run per segment: US large funding, US small funding, US leadership, Europe, central and eastern Europe, Asia-Pacific, Israel, Africa, Latin America, the rest of the world, and non-US leadership. The US rows are a chronological subset of the US family set assembled the same day. Amounts not stated in US dollars are converted at fixed approximate rates (EUR 1.10, GBP 1.30, NOK 0.095, INR 1 crore = USD 119,000, AUD 0.66, NZD 0.58) and the detail field keeps the amount as published, so an amount check should allow for currency rounding.
caveats: Many countries carry one or two events, so a country cell is an indication and not a rate; the regional totals are what can be read.

Coverage reflects which publishers allow an automated reader as much as where events happened: several national dailies, two large Asian and African startup outlets and some exchange portals refuse one, so their countries are under-represented and will look better covered than they are.

Latin America is thin (four events): the regional startup press for the month could largely not be verified from an allowed page with an in-window date, and several candidate pages turned out to be older articles re-dated in sitemaps.
Six funding rows are debt (securitisations, term loans, mezzanine), which some readers would not count as a funding round.
Funding rows with no published amount carry amount_disclosed=false and cannot contribute an amount defect either way.
The European rows overlap the Europe family set assembled the same day, so the two figures are not independent of each other.

132 of 152 items cite a publisher already in the tracker's source registry (data/feeds.csv or data/sources_catalogue.csv, checked 2026-11-11), because the publishers that allow an automated reader are largely the ones the tracker already collects from. Read the figure as recall within the publishers the tracker reads, not reach beyond them; the 20 items from other publishers are too few for a separate rate (10 of 20 held).
